question.problem:
Consider the matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 5 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}].$
Which of the following statements are true?

I. $B$ is upper triangular

II. $B$ is lower triangular

III. ${B}^{T}+B$ is upper triangular

current_example.problem:
Consider the matrix 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14251131/assets/1444afae9eb5ad7ffc8ca79ab9b0ea6efb7349d22e32c15e2aa9fe9942b57e8c.svg)
Which of the following statements are true?

I. $A$ is upper triangular

II. $A$ is lower triangular

III. $A^T-A$ is lower triangular
current_example.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false, since $A$ has non-zero entries below the main diagonal:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14251131/assets/a15beb9a72ac1f09a90d1a6323ec04b8d203724ba46429fa7c448e6c726cbac5.svg)

- Statement II is true, since all the entries above the main diagonal are zeros:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14251131/assets/f8fce80814ca28a566b48a0963f1ffe3dbc712cc7942de283aa43608c94b4080.svg)

- Statement III is false, since the result of $A^T-A$ has non-zero entries above the main diagonal:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14251131/assets/70d0d3b56788ac03a9dae7f05725d8d2c3354ac0cfa9e187321e515ef0018272.svg)

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only".
